meta.method: earned premium = annual premium × exposure (12-month term assumed); incurred proxy = paid, denied=0, open claims estimated from the paid/amount ratio of the same peril

signals.headline: Home insurance: claims consume 69% of written premium versus 38% for Auto.

exposureView.name: earned loss ratio (incurred proxy ÷ earned premium)

caveats: Paid ÷ written ignores unexpired premium and open claims; the earned view is on the same row.

signals.headline: Regional pricing: Ottawa (61%) and Montreal (55%) have the highest claims-to-premium ratios; Quebec City is lowest (37%).
caveats: City totals mix products: the cause sits in Home water (see the Montréal signals).

signals.headline: Distribution channel: broker policies cost 61.3% of premium in paid claims versus 43% Online and 42% Agent. Without broker B07 the broker figure is 45%.
caveats: One broker (B07) explains most of the gap; blaming the whole channel would be wrong.

signals.headline: Risk classification: Medium-risk policies cost 52% of premium vs 51% for High-risk (all lines). In Home the Medium band loss ratio is 1.29 vs 0.98 for High, so the bands look mis-priced.
caveats: Excludes broker B07. Bands are our own classification; Auto bands behave correctly (loss ratios 0.39/0.46/0.51).

signals.headline: Team C (Montreal + Quebec City) intake is 2.1× its earlier monthly pace (last 3 months 24, 22, 31 vs 12.4), holds 38 of 48 open claims and has the slowest median close (18 days).

signals.headline: Claim amounts bunch just under the $10,000 line (54 claims at $9–10k vs 15 at $10–11k); without the flagged brokers it is 25 vs 15.

signals.headline: Retention: customers whose claim took more than 30 days to close did not renew 55% of the time, versus 17% when it closed faster (84 vs 368 customers).

stats.test: two-proportion z-test at the best-separating cut-off (searched 10–30 days)

caveats: Cut-off was searched, so the effect size is optimistic; the monotone pattern across buckets is the safer evidence.
Observational: slow claims may also be bigger or harder claims.

signals.headline: Having a claim raises non-renewal from 15% to 24%; price level does not (non-renewal is 16–17% in every premium quartile).

signals.headline: Data quality: 140 premiums stored as text ("$1,046.62") and 108 dates in DD/MM/YYYY would silently distort totals; 15 duplicate claims and 11 city-label variants were cleaned.

home-vs-auto.title: Claims paid for every $1 of premium
home-vs-auto.plain: For every $1 of Home premium we pay about 69 cents in claims; for Auto only 38 cents.
home-vs-auto.how: Paid claims ÷ annual premium written, by product (policies.csv: policy_type, annual_premium; claims.csv: paid_amount joined by policy_id). The second bar uses premium actually earned so far.

home-bands.title: Home vs Auto: losses by risk band
home-bands.plain: In Auto, riskier bands cost more, as they should. In Home, the "Medium" band costs more than "High".
home-bands.how: Earned loss ratio = estimated claim cost ÷ earned premium, by risk_band, excluding broker B07.

city-water.title: Home water-damage claims per policy-year
city-water.plain: Montréal homes have water claims about 3 times as often as Toronto homes.
city-water.how: Water Damage claims on Home policies ÷ policy-years of exposure, by city (excluding broker B07).

water-months.title: Water claims by month of the year
water-months.plain: Montréal water claims peak in spring (March to May) and again in October. Toronto stays flat.
water-months.how: Count of Water Damage claims on Home policies by calendar month of loss_date (broker B07 excluded).

home-price-vs-cost.title: Home: what we charge vs what it costs, per year
home-price-vs-cost.plain: Our Home price barely changes from city to city, but the claims cost changes a lot.
home-price-vs-cost.how: Average earned premium and average estimated claim cost per policy-year, Home policies, by city (excluding broker B07).

b07-days.title: How many days after the policy starts do claims arrive?
b07-days.plain: Broker B07’s customers claim very soon after buying. Everyone else claims all year round.
b07-days.how: Days between policy start_date and claim loss_date, grouped; shown as a share of each group’s claims.

b07-amounts.title: How big are the claims? (note the $10,000 line)
b07-amounts.plain: Almost all of B07’s claims are just under $10,000, the amount where a senior person must review.
b07-amounts.how: claim_amount grouped in $1,000 steps, as a share of each group’s claims. Claims of $10,000 or more go to senior review.

brokers.title: Loss ratio by broker
brokers.plain: Nine brokers look normal. One (B07) loses about four dollars for every dollar of premium.
brokers.how: Estimated claim cost ÷ earned premium for each broker code (policies.csv: broker_code).

channels.title: Claims paid per $1 of premium, by sales channel
channels.plain: Brokers only look worse because of one broker. Without B07 they look like the other channels.
channels.how: Paid claims ÷ written premium by policies.csv channel; the second bar removes broker B07.

close-size.title: Days to close a claim: small vs big
close-size.plain: Claims of $10,000 or more take more than twice as long to close, in every team.
close-size.how: Median days between reported_date and closed_date by adjuster_team, for closed claims below and above $10,000.

team-intake.title: New claims per month, by team
team-intake.plain: Team C (Montréal and Québec City) has about twice as many new claims a month as before.
team-intake.how: Count of claims by reported_date month and adjuster_team (last 12 months). The latest month in the file may be incomplete.

wait-renewal.title: How long the claim took vs. did the customer renew?
wait-renewal.plain: When a claim takes more than 30 days, more than half of customers do not renew.
wait-renewal.how: For customers with a closed claim: share marked "Not Renewed" (policies.csv renewal_status), by days from reported_date to closed_date (the longest claim if several).

big-claims.title: Which claims are $10,000 or more?
big-claims.plain: One claim in ten is $10,000 or more, and they carry a third of all claim dollars. Almost half are water damage.
big-claims.how: Count of claims with claim_amount ≥ $10,000, by claim_type.

claim-types.title: Where the claim money goes
claim-types.plain: Water damage and theft are more than half of everything we pay.
claim-types.how: paid_amount summed by claim_type ÷ total paid.

cohorts.title: Is business getting worse? Loss ratio by year of sale
cohorts.plain: Business looks like it got worse in 2026, but it is one broker. Without B07, 2026 is normal.
cohorts.how: Earned loss ratio by policy start half-year, with and without the flagged broker.

bundle.title: Customers with both Auto and Home
bundle.plain: Customers who buy both Auto and Home claim less often.
bundle.how: Claims ÷ policy-years, split by whether the same customer_id holds both Auto and Home.
